context.checkin: I want to decide with my family. Please explain choices, not just one plan.

facts.value: Chronic heart failure (New York Heart Association Class III)
History of acute rheumatic fever (childhood, age 8)
Father: Hypertension, cerebrovascular accident at age 70
No family history of congenital heart disease or rheumatic fever
outpatient visit, Internal Medicine, Dr. James Okonkwo
Progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea for 6 months

She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. She reports a mild, persistent cough, especially when lying down, but denies any chest pain, palpitations, or lower extremity edema.
outpatient visit, Cardiology, Dr. Priya Sharma
Progressive shortness of breath and reduced exercise tolerance over the past year following recent hospitalization

The patient returns for follow-up of severe rheumatic mitral stenosis following January 2020 presentation. She presents with progressive shortness of breath and reduced exercise tolerance over the past year.
outpatient visit, Cardiology, Dr. Michael Chen
Worsening dyspnea on exertion progressing to shortness of breath at rest with ankle swelling

The patient returns for follow-up of rheumatic mitral stenosis, last evaluated in 2020, with progression of symptoms. She reports reduced exercise tolerance, difficulty climbing stairs, and waking up at night gasping for air.
outpatient visit, Cardiology, Dr. Priya Sharma
Progressive orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and episode of hemoptysis
She returns for follow-up of rheumatic mitral stenosis with progressive symptoms. She also reports a recent episode of coughing up a small amount of blood.
icu visit, Cardiology, Dr. Maria Gonzalez
Acute onset of shortness of breath, palpitations, and cough productive of pink, frothy sputum
Cardiology: Valve treatment options discussion (in 3 days)
